name: Paddle
tagline: Build a product catalog and entitlement layer around a normal payment provider

pricing.notes: No stable monthly plan; pricing is transaction based.

tiers.name: Pay as you go
tiers.limits: No published product or revenue cap; 5% + $0.50 per checkout; payments, billing, tax, fraud and chargeback handling included.

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.limits: Custom volume rates and commercial terms; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: No monthly fee and no published usage cap; Paddle charges 5% + $0.50 per checkout
pricing.billingTerms: transaction-only pricing; no monthly or annual subscription
pricing.hiddenCosts: Chargebacks cost $15 for cards or $20 for PayPal; Paddle itself adds no payout fee beyond the base rate, but the receiving bank or Payoneer can charge one.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Paddle, build a product catalog and entitlement layer around a normal payment provider. The hard boundary is merchant-of-record tax, billing, fraud, subscriptions, global payments, and compliance, plus payments, tax, distribution, and operations.
coreLoopDIY: Sell a small product catalog through a normal payment provider, deliver purchased files or lessons via an entitlement layer, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
whatYouLose: merchant-of-record tax, billing, fraud, subscriptions, global payments, and compliance
ongoingBurden: checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Paddle because creators pay to outsource the dangerous and tedious parts around money, delivery, tax, and customer access. The recurring cost buys checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Active open-source commerce platform with modular checkout and fulfillment primitives.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FOSSBilling
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Catalogs, subscriptions, downloads and licence keys fit, but the product remains explicitly beta with limited support.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A commerce backend can be extended into entitlements; that extension work is exactly what this exercise forbids.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Polar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The hosted path charges per sale and the self-hosted entitlement stack expects developers, not a non-builder.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Merchant of record plan and a single-creator storefront DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Paddle in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Stripe Checkout, and S3-compatible storage; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sell a small product catalog through a normal payment provider, deliver purchased files or lessons via an entitlement layer, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement products, variants, prices, files or lessons, coupons, customers, orders, and entitlements.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout and verify every webhook signature and idempotency key.
Grant access only after confirmed payment and revoke it on refund or chargeback.
Create a customer library with signed short-lived download or lesson URLs.
Add order search, resend receipt, refund handoff, export, and an immutable event log.
Document taxes as the creator's responsibility and do not calculate unsupported jurisdictions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out merchant-of-record tax remittance.
Deliberately leave out a buyer marketplace or affiliate network.
Deliberately leave out advanced communities, certificates, mobile apps, and enterprise learning features.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
